arjun: Heads-up — bringing up lumen-34b as a candidate for hosted catalog. Need a short quant plan (int8/fp8/gguf) and calibration checklist before we run full eval.

sophie: Agree. Can we do a quick sensitivity sweep first? i.e. layerwise scale + per-channel, and a fused-kernel run on H100 to check latency.

miguel: +1. Proposed steps:
1) small sensitivity sweep (1k prompts, 10 batches) for int8 with symmetric/asymmetric per-tensor vs per-channel
2) fp8 probe using dynamic range calibration (we have fp8 kernels in staging)
3) gguf export test for compatibility and size check

eva: For metrics, let's capture: perplexity (lm), token-level accuracy on closed tasks, embedding cos-sim drift on 2 eval sets, and a human A/B checklist for hallucination-sensitive prompts.

quant-bot: Note: default config will skip per-channel if model has > 64k params in layer_norm. Use --force-perchannel to override.

jen: Logistics: we should target A100-80GB for int8 smoke and H100 for fp8 latency numbers. Budget: 6 GPU-hours total for the sweep, then 24h for full calibration runs if results look good.

arjun: Good. For int8 calibration I suggest calibrating on a mixed-domain set: 40% code, 40% webQA, 20% dialogue. That gives realistic KV distribution.

sophie: Also include a small adversarial prompt bucket to catch decoding regressions (e.g., ambiguous instructions + chain-of-thought traps). We saw regressions on prior models with symmetric quantization.

miguel: Example commands for reproducibility:
```
calib-run --model lumen-34b --quant int8 --calib-set calib_mixed.json --batches 50 --per-channel true --seed 42 --out calib_int8_v1
calib-run --model lumen-34b --quant fp8 --calib-set calib_mixed.json --batches 20 --dynamic-range true --out calib_fp8_v1
gguf-export --model lumen-34b --quant-settings gguf-light.toml --out lumen-34b.gguf
```

eva: Add eval commands too:
```
eval-run --model lumen-34b:calib_int8_v1 --bench lm_perp.json --metrics perp,rouge,f1 --out eval_int8_smoke
eval-run --model lumen-34b:calib_fp8_v1 --bench embed_drift.json --metrics cos_sim,auc --out eval_fp8_smoke
```

quant-bot: Reminder: record kernel versions + CUDA/CuDNN + torch/TRT-like runtime tags in run metadata. These affect comparisons.

jen: Decision criteria proposal:
- If int8 loss < 1.5x FP32 loss on LM perplexity AND embedding cos-sim > 0.98 => accept int8 for hosted but enable fallback to fp8 for hallucination route.
- If fp8 gives <1.2x FP32 loss and latency improvement >20% over FP32 => prefer fp8 on H100 for high-throughput endpoints.
- If gguf export reduces size >2.5x with <2% quality drop on downstream metrics => add gguf artifact to model bundle.

arjun: Nice. Action items:
- miguel: run int8 sweep today (1k prompts, send results by EOD)
- sophie: prepare adversarial bucket and eval scripts
- eva: draft human A/B prompts and scoring sheet
- jen: reserve A100/H100 slots and attach billing tag

miguel: Starting sweep now. I'll post CSV of metrics + short notes when done. If I hit a weird layer with NaNs I'll tag @arjun.

sophie: I'll push the adversarial prompts to s3://redwood-ml/lumen_calib/ and share list once uploaded.

eva: For human A/B, using 50 prompts split across hallucination-sensitive/clarity/formatting. Will share rubric.

arjun: Thanks. If int8 looks rough we will try mixed-precision (fp8 in attention, int8 in MLP) — we've had good results before.

quant-bot: Run queued: calib-int8-2759000456 by miguel on a100-1 (ETA ~4m)

miguel: Run started. Will ping when CSV uploaded :eyes:
